reason: Cooling the lava and rock should help the surface retain liquid water, directly advancing the first goal.
expectation: The surface will lose heat to space and become cooler, though it may need further cooling before water can persist.

alternatives.reason: Cooler air could form clouds and rain, but the ground needs to cool to retain the water.

effect: The cool rock can already retain liquid water, so I can focus on making rain.
reaction: The contrast between cool rock and nearby boiling lava makes the uneven cooling clear.
reason: Cool air above the surface should help atmospheric water vapor condense into clouds.
expectation: I expect clouds or droplets to form, perhaps requiring another step to make rain reach the ground.

alternatives.reason: Radiating heat to space could also cool the atmosphere, but cooler air seems a more direct route to condensation.

effect: The vapor has condensed into clouds; gravity may now bring the droplets down as rain.
reaction: The distinction between clouds forming and the ground retaining water is useful.
reason: Combining the clouds with gravity seems the most direct way to make rain reach the ground.
expectation: I expect droplets to fall as rain, though some may boil away on the hotter lava.

alternatives.reason: Further atmospheric cooling might help, but the clouds have already formed.

effect: Rain is falling, but some may evaporate before reaching or remaining on the surface.
reaction: The possibility of rain evaporating in hot air adds a useful complication.
reason: I want to see what happens when the rain reaches the unevenly cooled coast.
expectation: Some rain may boil on the lava while water reaching cooler rock could remain liquid.

alternatives.reason: Cooling the atmosphere might also help rain survive, but the rain is already falling.

effect: The rain hit the hot patch and returned to the atmosphere as steam; the cooler rock can still retain water.
reaction: The result makes the contrast between neighboring patches clear, though I expected the rain might also reach cool rock.
reason: The only offered combination cools the atmosphere, which may help rain reach the ground.
expectation: I expect atmospheric heat loss to allow more rain to survive the descent, though another step may be needed.

effect: The atmosphere is cooling gradually as energy escapes, allowing the recycled steam to continue through the water cycle.
reaction: The coupled cooling of surface and atmosphere is a useful detail.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it may turn the recycled steam back into rain.
expectation: I expect the steam to condense again and perhaps produce rain that reaches the ground.

effect: The steam has joined a continuing cycle of evaporation and condensation; an enduring ocean has not yet formed.
reaction: Recycling the same water makes the earlier boiling feel consequential.
reason: The only offered combination uses cooler air to continue the cycle toward rain.
expectation: I expect the recycled water to condense and fall again, perhaps reaching the ground this time.

effect: More rain now survives its descent, so it can meet the cooled surface.
reaction: The gradual transition from recycled steam to persistent rain makes the cooling process clear.
reason: The only offered combination brings the rain to rock cool enough to retain liquid water.
expectation: I expect liquid water to collect on the cool rock and complete the rain goal.

effect: Rain remains liquid on the cool rock, completing the chapter’s goals and allowing water to accumulate in low ground.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the cooled surface finally retain the rain after the earlier recycling.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making rain return as steam on the hot lava made the contrast with neighboring cool rock concrete and showed that the water was recycled rather than lost.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequence of forced cooling and recycling combinations became somewhat repetitive, even though the explanations added useful detail.

surprise.text: Rain could boil away on one patch while nearby rock was already cool enough to retain liquid water.

arbitrary.text: The later recycling steps felt somewhat prescribed: they were the only offered combinations, so I followed them without making a meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because the contrast between cooling, rain and recycling made the natural processes understandable, though I would hope for more meaningful choices.
